notes:
[TXT032-strata] Manuscript page 31 continues the intersection/stratum argument from the previous page. For A∈F\G it says A∩B is a union of F strata, then reduces to expressing an F stratum as a union of F′ strata. The first case literally has A∉G′ and A∈F\G′⊂F′; both high primes are visible. The next case has A∈G and cites G′≼G. The cancelled union has the literal lower condition B≤F. These readings are retained despite the mathematical temptation to alter them. The opening says que une, without inserting an elision.

[TXT032-corollary] The corollary changes raffinement to subdivision and inserts chacune before the baseline des propriétés. Its article is Le. Condition a), a greatest-element assertion for the subdivisions inducing G′ on G, is crossed by a large X; maximal was also locally crossed and replaced by un plus grand followed by an uncertain element abbreviation. A separate margin reads Ultra faux. The starred gloss compares the two orders for subdivisions of the same figure, using literal equality/ditto signs twice.

[TXT032-margin] The long oblique note says that b), c), d) are equivalent and implied by a), that they characterize the constructed subdivision, and that they are far from implying a). Several small words and endings remain uncertain. The long curved stroke passes through successive words rather than outside the block: cancellation of the whole note is probable but not certain, so the complete text and the stroke are preserved with an explicit uncertainty about deletion state. The small initial a) is a distinct local cancellation. This is a record of the author’s revision, not a proof of the asserted equivalences or a refutation established by the editors.

[TXT032-bcd] Condition b) asks the canonical map F′→F to induce a bijection F′\G′→F\G; the right note asserts it is always surjective and singles out injectivity as what remains to prove here. Condition c) replaces a cancelled sentence by the assertion that every A∈F\G has its open stratum A-circle as an open F′ stratum. Condition d) is F′⊃F\G, restated pointwise. The proof still displays d)⇒b)⇒c)⇒a)⇒d); the later warning is not used to edit that chain. It starts d)⇒b) by identifying the restricted map with the canonical inclusion and reducing the task to F\G=F′\G′.

[TXT032-reduction] The main reader checked this last reduction only conditionally: if the restriction is the identity on F\G and its stated domain F′\G′ equals F\G, then that restriction is a bijection onto F\G. The required equality itself, the full stratum argument, and the four-way equivalence were not proved in this run.

[TXT032-literal-F-minus-Gprime] After the primes were read, a finite computation checked whether F\G′⊂F′ follows from the union construction and equal supports alone.
